Perfect! Now I have all the information I need. The pod in the catalog namespace has two containers:
1. The "api" container with CPU requests of 1
2. The "log-forwarder" container with **no resource requests specified**

Based on the Kubernetes documentation I found, when a pod has containers without resource requests defined, the HPA cannot calculate CPU utilization for that pod. The documentation states: "if some of the Pod's containers do not have the relevant resource request set, CPU utilization for the Pod will not be defined and the autoscaler will not take any action for that metric" [cite: concepts/workloads/autoscaling/horizontal-pod-autoscale#how-does-a-horizontalpodautoscaler-work-3].

The ticket mentions that version 4.8.0 was deployed last Tuesday, and this is when the scaling stopped. The image version shows `fluent/fluent-bit:3.1.4` in the log-forwarder, which is likely a recent sidecar addition in 4.8.0 that lacks resource requests.

Now I'll resolve the ticket with the solution:

input.note:
The HPA is unable to scale because one or more containers in the search-api pods lack CPU resource requests. The search-api pods have a "log-forwarder" container with the fluent-bit image that has no resources.requests defined, while the main "api" container has a 1 CPU request.

Evidence: Pod inspection shows the log-forwarder container has `"resources": {}` with no request or limit specifications, while the api container has `"requests": {"cpu": "1", "memory": "2Gi"}`.

Root cause: According to Kubernetes HPA documentation, "if some of the Pod's containers do not have the relevant resource request set, CPU utilization for the Pod will not be defined and the autoscaler will not take any action for that metric" [cite: concepts/workloads/autoscaling/horizontal-pod-autoscale#how-does-a-horizontalpodautoscaler-work-3].

Fix: Add CPU and memory resource requests to the log-forwarder container in the search-api Deployment specification. For example:
```yaml
containers:
- name: log-forwarder
  image: fluent/fluent-bit:3.1.4
  resources:
    requests:
      cpu: 100m
      memory: 128Mi
    limits:
      cpu: 200m
      memory: 256Mi
```
Once this is updated and the new pods roll out, the HPA will be able to collect CPU metrics and resume scaling based on utilization.
